title: UNIT 3: MOTION IN ONE AND TWO DIMENSIONS
notes: ✓ Kinematics → Describes the motion of objects using position, displacement, distance, speed, velocity and acceleration without focusing on the forces causing the motion.

title: 3.1 UNIFORMLY ACCELERATED MOTION IN 1D
notes:
✓ Motion in one dimension → Occurs along a straight line.

◆ BASIC QUANTITIES
✓ Position → Location of an object relative to a reference point.

✓ Distance → Total path length travelled; scalar.

✓ Displacement → Change in position; vector.

✓ Speed → Rate of change of distance; scalar.

✓ Velocity → Rate of change of displacement; vector.

✓ Acceleration → Rate of change of velocity; vector.

◆ ACCELERATION
✓ Average acceleration:

aₐᵥ = Δv/Δt = (Vf − Vi)/(tf − ti)

✓ Instantaneous acceleration → Acceleration at a particular instant:
a = lim(Δt→0) Δv/Δt

◆ IMPORTANT
✓ Negative acceleration → Does not always mean slowing down.

✓ Positive acceleration → Does not always mean speeding up.

✓ Speeding up or slowing down → Depends on the relative directions of velocity and acceleration.

title: 3.2 EQUATIONS OF UNIFORMLY ACCELERATED MOTION IN 1D
notes:
✓ For constant acceleration, the main kinematic equations are:

✓ vf = vi + at

✓ s = vi t + ½at²

✓ vf² = vi² + 2as

✓ s = [(vi + vf)/2]t

✓ s = vf t − ½at²

◆ Where:
s → Displacement
vi → Initial velocity
vf → Final velocity
a → Acceleration
t → Time

◆ AVERAGE VELOCITY FOR UNIFORM ACCELERATION
✓ Vav = (vi + vf)/2

✓ Key idea → These equations apply when acceleration remains constant. Choose the equation containing the known quantities and the required unknown.

title: 3.3 GRAPHICAL REPRESENTATION OF UNIFORMLY ACCELERATED MOTION IN 1D
notes:
✓ Motion can be represented using position/displacement-time, velocity-time and acceleration-time graphs.

◆ DISPLACEMENT-TIME (s–t) GRAPH
✓ Slope → Velocity.
✓ Horizontal line → Object at rest.
✓ Straight line with constant slope → Constant velocity.
✓ Increasing slope → Acceleration.
✓ Decreasing slope → Deceleration.

◆ VELOCITY-TIME (v–t) GRAPH
✓ Slope → Acceleration.
✓ Area under the graph → Displacement.

◆ ACCELERATION-TIME (a–t) GRAPH
✓ Shows how acceleration changes with time.
✓ Constant acceleration → Horizontal line.

◆ VERTICAL MOTION EXAMPLE
✓ For an object thrown upward → Velocity decreases to zero at maximum height, then becomes negative during downward motion.

✓ Key idea → Slope and area provide physical information:

s–t slope → Velocity.
v–t slope → Acceleration.
v–t area → Displacement.

title: 3.4 VERTICAL MOTION
notes:
✓ Vertical motion → Motion upward or downward under the influence of gravity.

◆ FREE FALL
✓ Free fall → Motion of an object vertically under gravity alone.

✓ The acceleration is constant and is called acceleration due to gravity, g.

◆ UPWARD-POSITIVE MOTION
✓ v = u − gt

✓ y = ut − ½gt²

✓ v² = u² − 2gy

✓ For downward-positive motion → The corresponding equations use +g.

◆ VERTICAL UPWARD MOTION
✓ At launch → Velocity is upward.
✓ During ascent → Velocity decreases because of gravity.
✓ At maximum height → v = 0.
✓ During descent → Velocity becomes downward.
✓ Acceleration → Remains downward and approximately g = 9.8 m/s².

◆ TERMINAL VELOCITY
✓ As a falling object speeds up → Air resistance increases.

✓ When air resistance balances weight → Net force becomes zero → Acceleration becomes zero → The object moves at constant maximum speed called terminal velocity.

◆ REACTION TIME & SAFETY
✓ Reaction time → The time taken to observe, think and respond to a sudden event.

✓ Reaction distance = Speed × Reaction time.

✓ Braking/stopping distance → Depends on speed, acceleration, friction and reaction time.

✓ Key idea → In ideal free fall, all objects have the same gravitational acceleration regardless of mass when air resistance is neglected.

title: 3.5 UNIFORM CIRCULAR MOTION
notes:
✓ Uniform circular motion → Motion along a circular path at constant speed while the direction of velocity continuously changes.

✓ Constant speed → Does not mean zero acceleration in circular motion because velocity changes direction.

◆ ANGULAR DISPLACEMENT
✓ Angular displacement → The angle swept out by the radius.

✓ θ = s/r

✓ s → Tangential displacement
✓ r → Radius

◆ ANGULAR VELOCITY
✓ Rate of change of angular displacement:
ω = Δθ/Δt

✓ Unit → rad/s.

◆ TANGENTIAL VELOCITY
✓ Velocity along the tangent to the circular path:
v = rω = 2πr/T

✓ T → Period.

◆ CENTRIPETAL ACCELERATION
✓ Acceleration directed toward the center of the circle:
aᶜ = v²/r = ω²r

✓ It changes the direction of velocity.

◆ CENTRIPETAL FORCE
✓ The force responsible for centripetal acceleration:
Fc = maᶜ = mv²/r = mω²r

✓ It always acts toward the center and is perpendicular to the instantaneous direction of motion.

◆ APPLICATIONS
Cars moving around curves/roundabouts.
Merry-go-rounds.
Objects rotated by strings.
Centrifuges.

✓ Key idea → Constant speed does not mean zero acceleration in circular motion because velocity changes direction.
